title: Permissionless pullAndRefresh enables window-stretching griefing that dilutes emission rate for existing stakers
description: pullAndRefresh() is external and has no access control. It forwards to _syncBudget(), which on ANY non-zero inflow from the dispatcher hook unconditionally performs `windowEnd = block.timestamp + windowDuration` and `rewardRate = rewardBudget / windowDuration`. Because the dispatcher hook (BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook) accrues mint-debt continuously block-by-block, `dispatcherHook.pull()` will return a non-zero amount on essentially every block. An adversary can therefore poke pullAndRefresh() whenever they choose, forcing a rate-recalculation that stretches the remaining budget over a fresh full `windowDuration` instead of the already-elapsed time. The net effect is a permanent reduction in `rewardRate` every time the attacker pokes, and the griefing is cheap because no deposit is required.
economicImpact: Attacker reduces the per-second reward rate paid to legitimate stakers, indefinitely. Every poke extends windowEnd back to `now + 540 days`, forcing the remaining budget to be smoothed over the new longer window. Repeated pokes compound the dilution because each call spreads a slightly-larger-but-still-small budget (previous budget minus elapsed accrual plus the tiny new inflow) over the full window again, so the effective emission is heavily back-loaded and the denial-of-rate can persist until the attacker stops.
attackPath:
1. Protocol runs for (say) 450 days of a 540-day window with rewardBudget originally 540e18. After 450 days ~ 90e18 remains, and rewardRate is the original 540e18/46,656,000 ~ 1.157e13 wei/sec.
2. Attacker calls pullAndRefresh(). dispatcherHook.pull() mints whatever mint-debt has accrued in the hook (call it `X`, often non-zero because phUSD accrues continuously on the hook side).
3. `_syncBudget` sees inflow > 0, sets windowEnd = now + 540 days, rewardRate = (90e18 + X) / 46,656,000 ~ 1.929e12 wei/sec, roughly 1/6 of the prior rate.
4. Attacker repeats every time meaningful mint-debt has re-accumulated (or just once a day). Each call re-stretches the still-largely-unspent budget back over 540 days.
5. Legitimate stakers receive a fraction of the emission they would have gotten under the original schedule; the remainder is back-loaded and can be captured by whoever stakes late.
6. Cost to attacker is one tx per poke (no deposit, no stake needed). Value extracted = time-value of the diluted emissions, plus a redistribution of rewards from long-term stakers to late/opportunistic stakers.
quantifiedLoss: Worst-case: if pullAndRefresh is called repeatedly at short intervals, the effective emission tends towards (budget + tiny_inflow) / windowDuration, so stakers can see their realized rate collapse to a small fraction of the original. Concrete example (540-day window, 90e18 remaining with 90 days left on the original schedule): original realized rate ~1.157e13 wei/sec; after one poke ~1.929e12 wei/sec — ~83% reduction in the rate stakers earn for the rest of the year. Repeated pokes keep the rate stuck at the diluted level.
recommendation: Restrict pullAndRefresh() to a trusted role (owner or keeper), AND do not reset the window on every inflow. Better alternatives: (a) only reset the window when the inflow exceeds some min-threshold (e.g. 1% of current budget); (b) only extend the window by `inflow / rewardRate` seconds (cap at windowDuration) rather than always resetting to `now + windowDuration`; (c) compute the new rate as `max(currentRate, (budget + inflow) / windowDuration)` and set `windowEnd = block.timestamp + (rewardBudget / newRate)` so that any inflow can only ever increase the rate, never decrease it. Also apply the same semantics to `topUp` (which today unconditionally resets the window too). Any of these breaks the griefing incentive while preserving the spec's stated 'window reset on inflow' intent.
mergeNote: ES-02 merged in: same root cause (unconditional window reset on ANY non-zero inflow dilutes remaining stakers). ES-02 covered the dust-inflow flavour (a 1e12 wei inflow at day 30 of a 540-day window silently stretches the schedule back to a fresh 540 days, costing stakers 30 days of budget-velocity) and highlighted that `topUp` has identical reset semantics to `_syncBudget` — so an owner running topUp with tiny amounts can keep the schedule in a perpetual reset state. ES-08 (MEV portion) merged in: searchers can front-run a victim's claim() with pullAndRefresh() to reset the window before the victim's claim lands, or back-run to capture the rate change; either flavour transfers value from long-term stakers to JIT stakers / searchers. The gas-externalisation sub-point of ES-08 was low-value and dropped.
